Raj (Sales): Heads-up — large prospect (FinServ) asked for a Dedicated pool that can sustain 2.5k concurrent requests for chat generation during market hours, with the ability to burst to 6k for short periods. They want predictable cost and an SLA. Can we size this and capture the tradeoffs?
Emily (PM): Thanks Raj. Do we have their expected tokens/sec or p95 latency target? Also any constraints on quantization/quality?
Raj (Sales): They expect ~10 tokens/request average, target 150ms p95 on shorter prompts (<=512 tokens). Quality: no aggressive quantization, prefer int8 if we validate output.
Marcus (Solutions): Quick back-of-envelope: 2.5k concurrent * 10 tokens/request = 25k tokens in flight. With our current perf on A100-80g ~ 30 tokens/s per GPU for that model @ int8-ish. So baseline GPUs required ~= ceil(25k / 30) = ~834 GPUs — that's huge. Burst to 6k concurrent -> ~2000 GPUs. We need autoscale + routing to cheaper model variant for bursts.
Ana (Eng-runtime): Marcus, can you share the perf numbers you used? We should consider batching efficiency and KV cache reuse; for chat workloads steady concurrency can improve tokens/s/GPU. Also option: keep a warmed pool for low-latency small requests, and route bulk to high-throughput instances.
Marcus (Solutions): Perf numbers: tested gpt-like-v1 on a100-80g, seq len 512, batch-opt: 30 tok/s/GPU @ 70% util. With continuous batching could hit ~45 tok/s/GPU but at cost of latency. So trade: higher per-GPU throughput vs p95 latency.
Leila (SRE): From reliability side, cannot commit to an SLA that depends on elastic burst 3x baseline unless we have reserved burst capacity or cross-region fallback. Also need a fallback policy: graceful degrade to smaller model variant or queueing with retry.
Emily (PM): Proposed approach for intake: 1) Capture customer constraints (p95 latency, quality/quantization, security). 2) Propose two configurations: "Low-latency pool" optimized for p95 and "High-throughput pool" optimized for cost. 3) Define rollout + acceptance criteria. Marcus/Ana, can you sketch config options and run approximate cost?
Marcus (Solutions): Draft configs:
```yaml
low_latency_pool:
  gpu_type: a100-80g
  gpus: 200
  target: p95 <= 200ms
  autoscale:
    min: 150
    max: 300
    burst_buffer: 150% # short spike handling
high_throughput_pool:
  gpu_type: a100-80g
  gpus: 700
  target_util: 70%
  autoscale:
    min: 500
    max: 1200
    scale_policy: gradual
routing:
  - priority: low_latency_pool
  - fallback: high_throughput_pool -> smaller_model_variant
```
This keeps baseline capacity to meet 2.5k concurrency (approx) across pools and allows ~6k burst with fallback. Need validation.
Ana (Eng-runtime): Notes: - burst_buffer 150% is an internal cache concept not hard cap; we should model queueing behavior. - We'll need to enable prefix KV caching for chat to reduce work per turn. - For autoscaling, prefer target_util over fixed % to avoid aggressive scale churn.
Raj (Sales): Customer expects cost estimate for both options. Can we provide monthly committed vs burst pricing? They like reserved capacity with a burst add-on.
Emily (PM): Acceptance criteria for product backlog item: 1) Sizing proposal with cost delta (reserved vs on-demand); 2) A fallback routing policy defined and implemented in config; 3) Autoscale policy with simulated behavior and no regressions on p95 in our load tests; 4) Runbook for SRE for burst events.
Leila (SRE): Add: automatic alarms for queue depth and token processing latency, and an automated rollback to smaller model if p95 > target for >2m. Also need runbook steps and who to page.
Marcus (Solutions): I'll produce a short deck with cost estimates and the above configs by EOD tomorrow.
Ana (Eng-runtime): I'll run a synthetic load sim for both pools on staging to validate p95 and throughput; ETA 2 days.
Emily (PM): Great — I'll create intake ticket and mark as high priority for dedicated-capacity backlog. Assigning to Marcus for sizing, Ana for perf validation, Leila for runbook. Raj, please add the customer's contract timeline in the ticket.
Raj (Sales): Will add timeline today. Thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment marker: scheduled pipeline for perf-sim started (ci/infra/perf-sim #482)
Leila (SRE): Quick question — do we need cross-region warm pools for their compliance? Raj, check if they require single-region data residency.
Raj (Sales): They require EU data residency, but want failover in another EU region. Not global.
Emily (PM): Noted. We'll include region constraints in the ticket.
Marcus (Solutions): One more: recommend model variant A for low-latency and variant B (quantized) for bursts. We'll validate quality differences against their prompt set during perf tests.
Emily (PM): Perfect. Moving to backlog now.
